edges.description: Loss of VPS13C lowers the mitochondrial membrane potential and fragments the mitochondrial network. VPS13C is partly present on the outer mitochondrial membrane but its principal contact site is ER-lysosome (VPS13A, not VPS13C, is the ER-mitochondria tether), so the route from the lysosomal contact site to this mitochondrial defect is not fully resolved.
Loss of VPS13C at ER-lysosome contact sites disrupts lysosomal lipid delivery, so lysosomes accumulate with an altered lipid profile.
The depolarized, damaged mitochondria are cleared by markedly increased PINK1/parkin-dependent mitophagy, with transcriptional upregulation of PARK2.
Chronic mitochondrial dysfunction in dopaminergic neurons drives their degeneration, as in the other mitochondrial recessive parkinsonisms.

Lysosomal dysfunction (with mitochondrial damage) leaves cytosolic mitochondrial DNA uncleared and blocks lysosome-dependent degradation of activated STING, activating the cGAS-STING innate-immune pathway.
cGAS-STING-driven innate-immune/neuroinflammatory signaling is a candidate contributor to dopaminergic neurodegeneration in VPS13C disease.
Loss of nigral dopaminergic neurons depletes striatal dopamine.

nodes.description: Because VPS13C is the lipid-transfer protein at ER-late endosome/lysosome contact sites, its loss disrupts lysosomal lipid delivery: lysosomes accumulate with an altered lipid profile, including di-22:6-BMP, a lipid biomarker shared with the LRRK2 G2019S form of Parkinson disease. This is the endolysosomal limb of VPS13C disease, complementary to the mitochondrial limb.

nodes.description: VPS13C loss lowers the mitochondrial membrane potential and fragments the mitochondrial network, with increased respiration rates — a bioenergetic and morphological mitochondrial defect shown in VPS13C-depleted cell models. This is the mitochondrial mechanism VPS13C shares with PRKN and PINK1, as distinct from the presynaptic endocytic mechanism of SYNJ1 and DNAJC6.

nodes.description: The root lesion is biallelic loss of VPS13C, which encodes a large lipid-transfer protein of the VPS13 family that mediates bulk transfer of glycerophospholipids between the endoplasmic reticulum and apposed organelle membranes at membrane contact sites. VPS13C tethers the ER principally to late endosomes/lysosomes (and to lipid droplets); an early cell-model report also found partial localization to the outer mitochondrial membrane. The causal alleles are truncating, consistent with loss of function.

nodes.description: VPS13C depletion activates the DNA-sensing cGAS-STING innate-immune pathway, driven by elevated cytosolic mitochondrial DNA together with a failure to degrade activated STING. cGAS-STING has been implicated in Parkinson pathogenesis, so this is a candidate neuroinflammatory contributor to degeneration; the evidence is from a human cell model, not yet confirmed in VPS13C patient dopaminergic neurons.
